mainTopic: The rules of reaping the עומר: reaping early for a מצוה, lessons from 'תקריב', whether an עומר reaped by day is valid, and why its reaping overrides שבת
overview: This amud first finishes an earlier point: רבי מאיר agrees with רבי עקיבא on one issue about cutting animal feed and disagrees on another. Then the גמרא explains the משנה. You may reap before the עומר for a מצוה need, because the פסוק says 'your harvest'. But you may not tie that grain into bundles, because we avoid extra work with the new grain. A ברייתא learns many rules from the word 'תקריב'. The עומר may come from cut sheaves or dry grain if nothing better is found, it is valid even if reaped by day, and it overrides שבת and טומאה. The גמרא then challenges the rule about reaping by day from a משנה in מגילה. רבה answers that our משנה follows רבי and the משנה in מגילה follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who builds his view on the rules of רבי עקיבא and רבי ישמעאל. Finally, the גמרא asks why רבי, a student of רבי שמעון, lets the reaping override שבת. It answers that he follows רבי שמעון's teaching that a מצוה done at its proper time is especially dear.

steps.title: רבי מאיר agrees with רבי עקיבא on one point and disagrees on another
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא settles the earlier question: רבי מאיר holds like רבי עקיבא in one case but argues with him in another.
steps.simpleTranslation: He agrees with him on one thing, and disagrees with him on one thing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a question from just before this point: is רבי מאיר simply saying the same thing as רבי עקיבא? The answer is that he agrees on one point and disagrees on another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both hold that cutting animal feed before it reaches a third of its growth does not count as the start of the harvest. They differ on feed that has already reached a third: רבי עקיבא says cutting it still does not count, while רבי מאיר says it does count as harvesting, so it does not split the field for פאה. Because they differ, the two opinions are not the same.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds like him (agrees with his view)
He disagrees with him
On one (point or issue)

phrases.english: He holds like him on one point,
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי מאיר and 'him' is רבי עקיבא, from the discussion just before this.

phrases.english: and disagrees with him on one point.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבַר לַהּ כְּוָותֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא, וּפְלִיג עֲלֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised just before this point about whether רבי מאיר's view is the same as רבי עקיבא's.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Partial agreement: the two views overlap in one case and differ in another
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have thought רבי מאיר's view adds nothing, since it matches רבי עקיבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר matches רבי עקיבא only for feed under a third of its growth, and differs for feed past a third, so his view is its own.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה on reaping early for a מצוה, and asking why
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's list of times when one may reap before the עומר, then asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may reap because of the saplings, because of the house of mourning, and because of the study hall. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes its rule that you may reap new grain before the עומר in three special situations. It then asks why this is allowed, which sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the new grain may not be reaped before the עומר is harvested. The משנה lists exceptions: reaping to protect young trees, to make room for comforting mourners, and to make room for Torah learning. The גמרא wants a source for why these exceptions are allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: One may reap (cut the grain)
Saplings, young trees
A house of mourning, where people come to comfort mourners
The study hall
What is the reason?

phrases.english: One may reap because of the saplings,
phrases.notes: The grain is growing next to young trees and would harm them.

phrases.english: and because of the house of mourning,
and because of the study hall.
phrases.notes: He means making room so that learning in the study hall is not held back.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for allowing reaping before the עומר in these situations.

steps.title: The פסוק says 'your harvest', not a harvest for a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The word 'קצירכם' limits the ban to a personal harvest, so קציר מצוה is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Merciful One said 'your harvest', and not a harvest done for a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק: the Torah says the עומר must come before 'your harvest', which means a harvest done for yourself, not one done for a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'your' shows that the rule is about reaping for your own benefit. Reaping to protect trees, comfort mourners, or make room for learning counts as קציר מצוה. So it falls outside the ban.

keyTerms.meaning: Your harvest (ויקרא 23:10)
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
Reaping done for the sake of a מצוה

steps.whatToRemember: Reaping before the עומר is only forbidden when it is 'your harvest' for yourself. Reaping for a מצוה need is allowed.

phrases.english: The Merciful One said 'your harvest',
and not a harvest for a מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״קְצִירְכֶם״ אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'קצירכם' limits the ban to a personal harvest, leaving out קציר מצוה.

steps.title: Why the cut grain may not be tied into sheaves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that the grain cut early may not be bound into sheaves, only left loose, and asks why.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he may not make bundles, but he leaves them in loose piles. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: even when reaping is allowed, you may not tie the grain into bundles. It asks why, which sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the reaping itself is allowed for a מצוה, the question is why binding the grain should be any different. The גמרא is looking for the reason behind this limit.

keyTerms.meaning: Bound bundles, sheaves
Loose handfuls or piles that are not tied
He leaves them (as they are)

phrases.english: And he may not make bundles,
but he leaves them in loose piles.
What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא יַעֲשֶׂה כְּרִיכוֹת, אֲבָל מַנִּיחָן צְבָתִים. מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the משנה's next rule, which limits the permission given in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why binding is forbidden when the reaping itself was allowed.

steps.title: We avoid extra work with the grain whenever we can
steps.stepSummary: Whatever work can be avoided with the new grain, we do not do.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because as much as is possible, we do not take the trouble.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the reaping was allowed only because of the מצוה need. Any extra work that isn't needed, like tying bundles, we avoid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The permission to reap only goes as far as the need. Tying the grain into sheaves is not needed for the מצוה, so we keep our handling of the new grain as small as possible.

keyTerms.meaning: As much as possible
We do not take the trouble (do extra work)

steps.whatToRemember: An allowance made for a מצוה goes only as far as needed. Extra handling of the new grain is still avoided.

phrases.english: Because as much as is possible, we do not take the trouble.
phrases.notes: He means we keep our handling of the new grain as small as we can.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּכַמָּה דְּאֶפְשָׁר לָא טָרְחִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: We avoid any unneeded work with the new grain, so binding is not allowed.

steps.title: The משנה: the עומר should come from standing grain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that the best way is to bring the עומר from grain still standing in the field.
steps.simpleTranslation: The מצוה of the עומר is to bring it from the standing grain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line of the משנה: the ideal way to do the מצוה of the עומר is to cut it from grain that is still growing. This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'מצות העומר' point to the preferred way of doing it. The question this raises, what happens if no standing grain is found, is answered by the ברייתא in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: The מצוה of the עומר (the preferred way to do it)
Standing grain, still growing in the field

phrases.english: The מצוה of the omer is to bring it from the standing grain.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִצְוַת הָעוֹמֶר לְהָבִיא מִן הַקָּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The best way to do the עומר is to bring it from standing grain.

steps.title: The ברייתא asks what the word 'תקריב' comes to teach
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks why the פסוק says 'ואם תקריב', and suggests it teaches what to do when no standing grain is found.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'And if you bring a meal offering of first fruits'. Why does the verse say this? Since the מצוה of the עומר is to bring it from standing grain, how do we know that if one does not find standing grain, he may bring it from sheaves?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that asks what extra lesson the פסוק about the מנחת בכורים is teaching. The ברייתא points the question at a case where no standing grain can be found, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ideal is standing grain, as the משנה said. The ברייתא asks where we learn that, when standing grain is missing, grain that was already cut and bundled is still allowed. It sets up the extra word in the פסוק as the source.

keyTerms.meaning: Meal offering of first fruits, here meaning the עומר (ויקרא 2:14)
What does the verse come to teach?
From where do we know?
Sheaves, grain already cut and bundled

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
'And if you bring a meal offering of first fruits',
what does the verse come to teach?

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁמִּצְוַת הָעוֹמֶר לְהָבִיא מִן הַקָּמָה,
phrases.english: Since the מצוה of the omer is to bring it from the standing grain,

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן שֶׁאִם לֹא מָצָא מִן הַקָּמָה
phrases.english: from where do we know that if he did not find standing grain
he may bring it from the sheaves?

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the משנה in step 6 and asks about the case where its ideal can't be met.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing the עומר may come from cut sheaves when no standing grain is found.

steps.title: The word 'תקריב' allows bringing from sheaves
steps.stepSummary: The extra word 'תקריב' teaches that the עומר may be brought from sheaves when there is no standing grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'you shall bring'.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question: the word 'תקריב' comes to include grain from sheaves that were already cut.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the פסוק adds the word 'תקריב', it widens the ways the עומר can be brought. Standing grain is still best, but grain from sheaves also works when no standing grain can be found.

keyTerms.meaning: You shall bring, the word used here to include more cases

steps.whatToRemember: The ideal way is to bring the עומר from standing grain. If none can be found, it may be brought from sheaves already cut, based on the word 'תקריב'.

phrases.english: The verse says 'you shall bring'.
phrases.notes: The word 'you shall bring' appears again in the same פסוק, ויקרא 2:14, and that extra word is what teaches the rule.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״תַּקְרִיב״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ברייתא's question from step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'תקריב' includes bringing the עומר from cut sheaves when no standing grain is found.

steps.title: Second lesson from 'You shall bring': dry grain is allowed
steps.stepSummary: Another explanation of 'תקריב': the עומר should be brought from fresh grain, but if none is found, dry grain may be used.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: 'You shall bring.' The מצוה is to bring the עומר from fresh (moist) grain. How do we know that if there is no fresh grain, he may bring it from dry grain? The פסוק says 'You shall bring.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second answer to its question of why the פסוק adds the word 'תקריב'. This time the extra word allows dry grain when no fresh grain can be found.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 8, 'תקריב' allowed sheaves when there was no standing grain. Here the same word allows a second fallback: dry grain when fresh grain is missing. The pattern is the same: there is a best way, and the extra word allows a backup.

keyTerms.meaning: Another explanation; a second way to read the same פסוק
Moist, fresh grain
Dry grain
The פסוק teaches; introduces the source of a rule

phrases.english: Another explanation: "You shall bring"
phrases.notes: This is the same word from ויקרא 2:14 that the ברייתא has been explaining since step 7.

phrases.english: since it is a מצוה to bring from the moist grain,

phrases.aramaic: וּמִנַּיִן שֶׁאִם לֹא מָצָא מִן הַלַּח
phrases.english: from where do we know that if he did not find any moist grain
he should bring from the dry grain?
The verse says: "You shall bring."

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: ״תַּקְרִיב״ – לְפִי שֶׁמִּצְוָה לְהָבִיא מִן הַלַּח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to step 7's question about the extra word 'תקריב'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'תקריב' allows bringing the עומר from dry grain when no fresh grain is available.

steps.title: Third lesson from 'You shall bring': reaping by day is valid
steps.stepSummary: Another explanation of 'תקריב': the עומר should be reaped at night, but if it was reaped by day it is still כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: 'You shall bring.' The מצוה is to reap the עומר at night. How do we know that if it was reaped by day it is כשר? The פסוק says 'You shall bring.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a third reading of 'תקריב'. This time the word teaches that an עומר reaped during the day is still valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The best way is to reap at night, but the extra word allows daytime reaping after the fact. This is the rule that the גמרא will soon challenge in step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: To reap or cut the grain
At night
Valid, acceptable

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule, that reaping by day is כשר, is the exact point the גמרא challenges from a משנה in מגילה in steps 12 and 13.

phrases.english: Another explanation: "You shall bring"
since its מצוה is to be reaped at night,
from where do we know that if it was reaped by day it is valid?
The verse says: "You shall bring."

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: ״תַּקְרִיב״ – לְפִי שֶׁמִּצְוָתוֹ לִקְצוֹר בַּלַּיְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third reading of the same extra word 'תקריב'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'תקריב' teaches that an עומר reaped by day is כשר.

steps.title: More rules learned from 'You shall bring'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists more lessons from 'תקריב': the עומר overrides שבת, may be brought in any form, from any place, on שבת, and even in טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know the עומר overrides שבת? The פסוק says 'You shall bring.' 'You shall bring': in any way it is found. 'You shall bring': from any place. 'You shall bring': even on שבת. 'You shall bring': even in טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with a quick list of rules, all hanging on the same word 'תקריב'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'תקריב' is read as a strong command: the עומר must be brought no matter what. So it pushes aside שבת and טומאה, and it does not have to come from the best grain or the usual place.

keyTerms.meaning: Overrides שבת; may be done even though it is normally forbidden on שבת
In any way or form at all
From any place
Ritual impurity

steps.whatToRemember: One word, 'תקריב', teaches many things: sheaves, dry grain, reaping by day, overriding שבת, any form, any place, and even in טומאה. The עומר must be brought no matter what.

phrases.english: And [from where do we know] that it overrides Shabbat?
phrases.notes: The words 'from where do we know' are not written here, but they are carried over from the earlier lines.

phrases.english: The verse says: "You shall bring."
"You shall bring": in any manner,
"You shall bring": from any place,
"You shall bring": even on Shabbat,
"You shall bring": even in ritual impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדוֹחָה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת, תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״תַּקְרִיב״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא's list of lessons from 'תקריב'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because of 'תקריב', the עומר overrides שבת and טומאה and may be brought in any form and from any place.

steps.title: Challenge: a משנה says night מצוות belong to the night
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that an עומר reaped by day is כשר, then raises a משנה in מגילה that lists reaping the עומר as a night-time מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה says: if it was reaped by day, it is כשר. But we learned in a משנה: the whole night is valid for reaping the עומר and for burning fats and limbs. This is the rule: something whose מצוה is by day is valid all day, and something whose מצוה is at night is valid all night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a contradiction between our משנה and a משנה in מגילה. The full force of the challenge comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה allows reaping by day. The other משנה puts reaping the עומר in the group of night-time מצוות and compares night מצוות to day מצוות. That comparison is what the גמרא will use to attack.

keyTerms.meaning: To burn on the מזבח
The fats of a קרבן that are burned on the מזבח
The limbs of a קרבן עולה
This is the general rule

phrases.english: If it was reaped by day, it is valid.
But didn't we learn: the whole night is valid
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in מגילה 20b.

phrases.english: for reaping the omer,
and for burning fats and limbs.
This is the rule:

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר שֶׁמִּצְוָתוֹ כׇּל הַיּוֹם – כָּשֵׁר כׇּל הַיּוֹם,
phrases.english: something whose מצוה is during the day is valid the whole day,

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר שֶׁמִּצְוָתוֹ בְּלַיְלָה – כָּשֵׁר כׇּל הַלַּיְלָה.
phrases.english: something whose מצוה is at night is valid the whole night.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִקְצַר בַּיּוֹם – כָּשֵׁר. וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the ברייתא's lessons back to the משנה's rule about reaping by day, which step 10 also taught, and opens a challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that an עומר reaped by day is כשר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה in מגילה lists reaping the עומר as a night-time מצוה, set side by side with day-time מצוות.

steps.title: The comparison shows a night מצוה done by day is not valid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sharpens the challenge: since the משנה compares night מצוות to day מצוות, a night מצוה done by day should be invalid, just like a day מצוה done at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה teaches night just like day. Just as a day מצוה is not valid at night, so too a night מצוה is not valid by day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its challenge by drawing a clear conclusion from the משנה in מגילה. רבה answers it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A day מצוה done at night is plainly invalid. Because the משנה puts night and day side by side, a night מצוה like reaping the עומר should also be invalid by day. That contradicts our משנה, which says reaping by day is כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Similar to; compared to
Just as ... so too ...; a way of making a comparison
Also not

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה in מגילה never says outright that a night מצוה is invalid by day. The גמרא is drawing that from the way the משנה compares night to day.

phrases.english: It teaches night similar to day:
just as a day מצוה is not valid at night,
so too a night מצוה is also not valid by day.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָתָנֵי לַיְלָה דּוּמְיָא דְּיוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge begun in step 12 by drawing the inference from the משנה in מגילה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that an עומר reaped by day is כשר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Night is compared to day. A day מצוה done at night is invalid, so a night מצוה like reaping the עומר should be invalid if done by day.

steps.title: רבה: the two משניות follow two different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that our משנה follows רבי, and the משנה in מגילה follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: There is no contradiction. This משנה follows רבי, and that משנה follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from steps 12-13. Each משנה follows a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two משניות don't need to agree. Our משנה (day-reaping is כשר) follows רבי. The משנה in מגילה (a night מצוה done by day is invalid) follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. The next steps prove that these two תנאים really disagree on this point.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
This one ... and that one; each source follows a different opinion

phrases.english: Rabba said: It is not difficult.
This one is Rabbi,
phrases.notes: "This one" is our משנה, which says an עומר reaped by day is כשר.

phrases.english: and that one is Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon.
phrases.notes: "That one" is the משנה in מגילה from step 12.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא רַבִּי, וְהָא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא raised in steps 12-13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning each source to a different תנא (מחלוקת תנאים)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות seemed to follow one view, so they contradicted each other
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה follows רבי (day-reaping is כשר). The משנה in מגילה follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון (day-reaping is פסול).

steps.title: The ברייתא: רבי says to bring a replacement עומר
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא about an עומר that became טמא shows that רבי allows reaping a new עומר right away, by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: If a כהן was offering the עומר and it became טמא, then if there is other grain, we tell him: bring another in its place. If not, we tell him: be smart and keep quiet. These are the words of רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה brings a ברייתא to prove that רבי allows reaping the עומר by day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עומר became טמא during the offering, which happens in the daytime. רבי says to bring a replacement if more grain is available. That replacement would have to be reaped right then, by day, so רבי must hold that a day-reaped עומר is כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: The עומר meal-offering of barley, brought on the 16th of ניסן
It became ritually impure (טמא)
In its place, as a replacement
Be smart and keep quiet: offer it and don't tell anyone it became טמא

phrases.english: As it is taught: If he was standing and offering
the עומר meal-offering, and it became impure,
if there is another, one says to him:
phrases.notes: "Another" means more barley that could still be reaped now.

phrases.english: "Bring another in its place,"
and if not, one says to him:
"Be smart and keep quiet,"
these are the words of Rabbi.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: הָיָה עוֹמֵד וּמַקְרִיב מִנְחַת הָעוֹמֶר וְנִטְמֵאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for רבה's claim about רבי
steps.raayaObject: That רבי holds an עומר reaped by day is כשר
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא (תוספתא) about an עומר that became טמא in the middle of the offering

steps.title: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון: an עומר not reaped properly is invalid
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says never reap a replacement, because an עומר reaped not according to its מצוה is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says: Either way, I tell him: be smart and keep quiet, because any עומר that was reaped not according to its מצוה is פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second half of the ברייתא. It shows that רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון disagrees and holds that a day-reaped עומר is invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even when more grain is available, he does not allow reaping a replacement. That reaping would happen by day, which is not the proper way to reap the עומר. This matches the משנה in מגילה, so רבה's answer is proven.

keyTerms.meaning: Either way; in both cases
Not according to its מצוה; not done the proper way
Invalid

steps.whatToRemember: רבי holds that a day-reaped עומר is כשר, and our משנה follows him. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון holds it is פסול, and the משנה in מגילה follows him.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon says:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ, אוֹמַר לוֹ:
phrases.english: Either way, I say to him:
"Be smart and keep quiet,"
because any עומר that was reaped
not according to its מצוה is invalid.
phrases.notes: Its מצוה is to be reaped at night, so reaping it by day makes it invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא by giving the opposing view
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון holds a day-reaped עומר is פסול
steps.raayaSupportSource: The second half of the same ברייתא

steps.title: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון follows רבי עקיבא's rule about שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's view is based on רבי עקיבא's rule: any מלאכה that could be done before שבת does not override שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון said this following the approach of רבי עקיבא, his father's teacher. As we learned: רבי עקיבא stated a rule: any מלאכה that could be done before שבת does not override שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining where רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's strict view comes from. It brings the first of two building blocks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first building block is רבי עקיבא's rule: a מצוה overrides שבת only if it truly could not have been done earlier. The second building block comes in the next step. Together they show that reaping the עומר has a fixed time that cannot be moved.

keyTerms.meaning: Following the approach or system of
His father's teacher (רבי עקיבא taught רבי שמעון)
A general rule
Does not override שבת

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon

phrases.aramaic: בְּשִׁיטַת רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא רַבּוֹ שֶׁל אָבִיו אֲמָרָהּ,
phrases.english: said it following the approach of Rabbi Akiva, his father's teacher,
as we learned: Rabbi Akiva stated a rule:
any labor that it is possible for him
to do before שבת
does not override שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּשִׁיטַת רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא רַבּוֹ שֶׁל אָבִיו אֲמָרָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the basis of the view quoted in step 16
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's view rests on רבי עקיבא's rule that a מלאכה that could be done before שבת does not override שבת

steps.title: He also holds like רבי ישמעאל that reaping the עומר is a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון also holds like רבי ישמעאל, who learns from a פסוק that reaping the עומר is a מצוה and overrides שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he holds like רבי ישמעאל, who said reaping the עומר is a מצוה. As we learned: רבי ישמעאל says: just as plowing is optional, so too reaping is optional. This excludes reaping the עומר, which is a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds the second building block of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's view: reaping the עומר is a מצוה, so it overrides שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says that on שבת you must rest from plowing and reaping. רבי ישמעאל says this means optional plowing and reaping, so the reaping of the עומר, which is a מצוה, is allowed on שבת. Put this together with רבי עקיבא's rule: since reaping the עומר overrides שבת, it must be something that cannot be moved to another time, so an עומר reaped outside its proper time is פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: The reaping of the barley for the עומר
Plowing
Optional; not a מצוה
Excluded; this case is left out of the rule

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's strict view combines two ideas: (1) רבי עקיבא: only something that cannot be done earlier overrides שבת; (2) רבי ישמעאל: reaping the עומר is a מצוה that overrides שבת.

phrases.english: And he holds like Rabbi Yishmael,
who said that reaping the עומר is a mitzva,
as we learned: Rabbi Yishmael says:
just as plowing is optional,
phrases.notes: He is explaining שמות 34:21, "בחריש ובקציר תשבת," which he reads as being about שבת.

phrases.english: so too the reaping is optional reaping,
which excludes reaping the עומר, which is a mitzva.
phrases.notes: So reaping the עומר is allowed even on שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, דְּאָמַר קְצִירַת הָעוֹמֶר מִצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the second source that רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון relies on
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reaping the עומר is a מצוה that overrides שבת (רבי ישמעאל). Together with רבי עקיבא's rule, this shows the reaping has a fixed time.

steps.title: Overriding שבת proves a wrongly-reaped עומר is invalid
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון reasons this way: if an עומר reaped not by its מצוה were כשר, there would be no need to override שבת. So it must be פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think an עומר reaped not the proper way is valid, why does reaping it override שבת? Just reap it on Friday! Since it does override שבת, that proves an עומר reaped not the proper way is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון put together רבי עקיבא's rule with רבי ישמעאל's view. Together they lead to his ruling that a replacement עומר is never reaped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's rule says that work which could be done before שבת does not override שבת. רבי ישמעאל teaches that reaping the עומר does override שבת. The only way both can be true is if reaping before שבת would not work, which means an עומר reaped not at its proper time is פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: It would enter your mind; you might think
Not according to its proper מצוה procedure
Overrides שבת
Friday, the day before שבת
Learn from this; this proves it

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, the fact that reaping the עומר overrides שבת is itself the proof that an עומר reaped at the wrong time is פסול.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that one reaped not according to its מצוה is fit,
why does it override Shabbat?
Let one reap it from Shabbat eve!
phrases.notes: This is רבי עקיבא's rule from Step 17: whatever could be done before שבת does not push off שבת.

phrases.english: Rather, from the fact that it overrides Shabbat, learn from it:
one reaped not according to its מצוה is unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ נִקְצַר שֶׁלֹּא כְּמִצְוָתוֹ כָּשֵׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation begun in Steps 17-18 by showing how the two premises combine.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's ruling that an עומר reaped not by its מצוה is פסול.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Logical inference from רבי עקיבא's rule together with רבי ישמעאל's view that reaping overrides שבת.

steps.title: Isn't רבי also a student of רבי שמעון?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי's view. As a student of רבי שמעון, he should accept רבי עקיבא's rule, so how can reaping override שבת if he holds a daytime עומר is כשר?
steps.simpleTranslation: And isn't רבי a student of רבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem with רבי's opinion from Step 15, using his teacher's tradition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי holds that an עומר reaped by day is fine. רבי עקיבא's rule, which comes down through רבי שמעון, says work that could be done earlier does not override שבת. So if רבי follows his teacher, reaping the עומר should not override שבת. He could simply reap it on Friday.

keyTerms.meaning: His student
Is he not...? (a question expecting the answer yes)

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי, לָאו תַּלְמִידֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הוּא?
phrases.english: And Rabbi, is he not a student of Rabbi Shimon?
phrases.notes: The point is that רבי שמעון learned from רבי עקיבא, so רבי should follow רבי עקיבא's rule from Step 17.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי, לָאו תַּלְמִידֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the reasoning of Step 19 against רבי, who disagrees with רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's position that an עומר reaped by day is כשר, while its reaping still overrides שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: As a student of רבי שמעון, רבי should hold רבי עקיבא's rule. Under that rule, a daytime-valid עומר could be reaped on ערב שבת, so its reaping should not override שבת.

steps.title: Source showing that רבי learned from רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records רבי describing how he studied with רבי שמעון in תקוע and carried oil and a towel for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said: When we studied Torah with רבי שמעון in תקוע, we carried oil and a towel for him from the courtyard to the roof, from the roof to an enclosure, and from one enclosure to another, until we reached the spring where we bathed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its claim that רבי really was רבי שמעון's student by quoting רבי's own memory of learning with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story shows that רבי was close to רבי שמעון and personally served him. That strengthens the question: רבי should be following his teacher's tradition.

keyTerms.meaning: A towel
A courtyard
An enclosed area, like a fenced yard
A spring

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: Rabbi said:
When we were learning Torah
with Rabbi Shimon in Tekoa,
we would bring up for him oil and a towel
from courtyard to roof, and from roof to an enclosure,
and from enclosure to another enclosure,
until we would reach the spring
that we would bathe in.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי: כְּשֶׁהָיִינוּ לְמֵדִין תּוֹרָה אֵצֶל רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בִּתְקוֹעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the claim in Step 20.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that רבי was a student of רבי שמעון.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי describes learning with and serving רבי שמעון in תקוע.

steps.title: רבי follows רבי שמעון's teaching that a מצוה at its time is dear
steps.stepSummary: רבי holds like another teaching of רבי שמעון: a מצוה at its proper time is so precious that we do not delay it. That is why the burning of fats and limbs was not pushed off until after שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי holds like the other teaching of רבי שמעון. רבי שמעון said: Come and see how dear a מצוה is at its proper time. Burning fats and limbs is valid all night, yet they would not wait until dark to burn them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question on רבי. His reason for letting the reaping override שבת is a different one from רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי agrees that a daytime עומר is כשר. Still, the proper time for reaping is at night, and a מצוה at its proper time is precious, so reaping at night overrides שבת. The proof is the burning of fats and limbs: on שבת they were burned right away, even though waiting until night would also have been valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the other (teaching or opinion)
A מצוה is dear when done at its proper time
Burning the fats and limbs of offerings on the מזבח
Until it gets dark

steps.whatToRemember: There are two reasons the עומר's reaping overrides שבת. For רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, a wrongly reaped עומר is פסול. For רבי, a מצוה at its proper time is precious, even though a later or earlier time would still be valid.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי now holds a daytime עומר is פסול. He still says it is כשר. He only says the proper time is so valued that reaping then overrides שבת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a מצוה can override שבת for two different reasons: because doing it another way would be invalid, or because its proper time is especially precious.

phrases.english: He holds like the other teaching of Rabbi Shimon,
as it is taught: Rabbi Shimon said:
Come and see how dear
is a מצוה in its time,
for burning of fats and limbs
is valid all night,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא הָיָה מַמְתִּין לָהֶן עַד שֶׁתֶּחְשַׁךְ.
phrases.english: and yet one would not wait with them until it gets dark.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבַר לַהּ כְּאִידַּךְ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Steps 20-21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different underlying reason: רבי relies on another teaching of the same teacher.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: As רבי שמעון's student, רבי should hold that reaping the עומר cannot override שבת if it could be reaped on ערב שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי follows רבי שמעון's principle that a מצוה at its proper time is dear. So the night reaping overrides שבת even though a daytime עומר is כשר.
